- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too high after sharp historical spikes, then overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends or when recent history shows mean reversion.
- Forecast bias is stronger when historical prices are high (e.g., >80) — model often fails to capture downward momentum.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — true values often dip below forecast before model adjusts.
- Forecasts show persistent overconfidence in upward momentum, even when recent data suggests consolidation or decline.
- When history includes a strong recent peak, model tends to overreact with a high forecast, then underreacts in subsequent days.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or cyclical patterns — e.g., price often drops after a high in late February, but forecast doesn’t reflect this.
- Forecast error is more severe when true outcome is below 70 — model often ignores downward pressure.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates sharp drops and overestimates gradual declines.
